title: Escapewheel adapter declaration document
description: Shape of the document an adapter a build cannot import publishes, per Part 12 §7. It carries what belongs to the adapter and nothing that belongs to the machine: the command, the root and the options stay in the recipe, because which interpreter is installed where is the recipe author's fact and the resources an adapter can supply is not. An implementation shipping both a document and an importable class generates the document rather than maintaining it.

$schema.description: This document's meta-schema, by $id: identity rather than a fetch instruction, so a build neither dereferences nor requires it.

kind.description: The name a recipe's source entry uses for this adapter.

protocols.description: Every protocol this adapter supports, any of which a build may reach it by (Part 12 §3). Membership of a group is the profile's to settle and a build's to refuse, so the pattern here fixes the shape and not the vocabulary.

items.description: A dotted resource ID some loaded registry declares.

produces.description: What this adapter can supply, whatever a given root happens to hold. A build settles ownership from it before any source is opened (Part 05 §3.4).

items.description: A dotted resource ID this adapter also names under `produces`.

contributes.description: The resources whose rows this adapter supplies only in part, such as the clocks of its own streams, which a source entry without `owns` contributes rather than owns (Part 05 §3.4). A build refuses one naming a resource `produces` does not (Part 12 §7).

needs.description: Every value a build supplies this adapter, each resolving against Part 12 §4's terms first and the recipe's options second. A term a protocol requires is not declared here: the protocol a build reaches the adapter by is what asks for it.

accepts.description: The options this adapter reads and can be constructed without, which a recipe may leave unset, and `source_cache` where the adapter keeps source data in the build's source-cache location (Part 12 §4). No other term may appear here, and no name here may also appear in `needs`.

states.description: The recipe fields this source can state, which a build compares against what the recipe declares (Part 05 §3.6). The values need the source read, so they travel under `stated` in the run's report (Part 12 §9) rather than here.

consumes.description: The kinds whose output this adapter reads, which orders a build rather than being passed to it.
